normative_evidence.document_name: OPC UA for Robotics — Part 1: Vertical Integration
normative_evidence.scope: Vertical integration information model for robot and motion-device-system state
normative_evidence.explicitly_out_of_scope: No evidence reviewed here shows that the information model itself actuates a safety-rated stop or replaces the robot safety controller
normative_evidence.rmos_use_boundary: Within the five D-03/D-08 objects reviewed in the historical package, this specification explicitly models EmergencyStop and ProtectiveStop separately. The finding is limited to that reviewed set and must not be generalized to industry uniqueness or physical actuation.

supported_atomic_facts: EmergencyStop and ProtectiveStop are separate modeled states
State model can expose vendor-specific stop functions
withdrawn_conclusions: Information-model state equals physical safety actuation
Historical ISO reference is sufficient current compliance basis

rmos_decision_fields.stack_gap: Information model versus Python application and manufacturer safety controller
failure_modes: Treating observed state as a command
Using a companion specification as the safety function
Generalizing beyond the reviewed object set
rmos_decision_fields.exit_strategy: Keep physical safety in applicable standards and manufacturer layer
alternative_candidates: OPC UA Safety when safety communication is actually proposed
